result.summary: The image shows a wide urban street with a well-maintained, wide sidewalk buffered from traffic by a row of parked cars and a green-painted bike lane. While the pedestrian walkway is high quality, the lack of visible crossing infrastructure and the wide roadway suggest a focus on vehicle throughput.

hazards.name: Wide Roadway
hazards.description: The wide, straight roadway may encourage vehicle speeds that are unsafe for an urban residential/commercial context.

hazards.name: Visual Obstructions
hazards.description: Parked cars along the curb can obscure pedestrians, especially children, from the view of oncoming drivers.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions at potential crossing points to shorten the crossing distance and improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Mid-block Crossing

interventions.title: Traffic Calming
interventions.description: Introduce vertical or horizontal deflections like speed tables or chicanes to manage vehicle speeds.

result.summary: The image depicts a wide, multi-lane arterial road with a car-centric environment and minimal pedestrian infrastructure. Pedestrians face long unprotected crossing distances and frequent conflict points due to large commercial driveways and a lack of marked crossings.

hazards.name: Excessive Crossing Distance
hazards.description: Pedestrians must cross four lanes of traffic without a marked crossing or median refuge.

hazards.name: Multiple Driveway Conflicts
hazards.description: Large curb cuts for the gas station and parking areas create frequent vehicle-pedestrian conflict points.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Install a raised median island to allow pedestrians to cross one direction of traffic at a time.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalk
interventions.description: Add a marked mid-block crossing with high-visibility paint and signage.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the roadway at crossing points to shorten the crossing distance and improve sightlines.

result.summary: The street features a buffered bike lane and a well-maintained sidewalk adjacent to modern mixed-use development. However, the multi-lane configuration and the placement of the bike lane between travel lanes create potential conflict points for vulnerable road users.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Parked Vehicles
hazards.description: Large parked vehicles, such as the black pickup truck, block sightlines between the sidewalk and the travel lanes.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the image, along the curb.

hazards.name: Weaving Conflict Point
hazards.description: The bike lane is positioned between a dedicated right-turn lane and through-traffic lanes, forcing vehicles to cross the bike path to turn.
hazards.location_in_image: Center-left, where the green bike lane is flanked by travel lanes.

hazards.name: Wide Crossing Distance
hazards.description: The multi-lane roadway creates a long, unprotected crossing distance for pedestrians at the upcoming intersection.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs at the intersection to shorten pedestrian crossing distances and improve visibility between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: Protected Bike Lane
interventions.description: Replace flexible delineator posts with concrete barriers or planters to provide physical protection for cyclists.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Apply continental-style pavement markings at the intersection to increase the visibility of the pedestrian crossing area.

result.summary: The image shows a wide, well-maintained concrete sidewalk in front of a modern mixed-use building with active ground-floor retail. A young street tree provides a minimal buffer, but there is no substantial physical separation between the pedestrian walkway and the adjacent roadway. The environment is generally pedestrian-friendly with clear sightlines and a clean walking surface.

hazards.name: Lack of physical protection
hazards.description: Pedestrians are separated from moving traffic only by a standard curb, with no bollards or substantial physical barriers to prevent vehicle incursions.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the curb line adjacent to the parked silver car in the foreground.

interventions.title: Install Bollards or Planters
interventions.description: Adding physical barriers like bollards or large planters along the curb would provide a protective buffer for pedestrians from potential vehicle incursions.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Implementing curb extensions at the nearest intersection or mid-block would shorten crossing distances and help slow traffic speeds.
